activity_summary: James Burbage said he could build a heavens for five pound, if he had five pound and a lease. He has the sentence, and not the money. Pope proposed they lower Kemp. Burbage looked at you and did not answer. Kemp asked to be winched down on a barrel. You said a boy and two men with clean verse can build a castle out of air, and it costs nothing to strike. You said again that the king's parts are not cast. No one agreed to build, to buy a lease, or to lower anyone.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Refused the rope, repeated that the parts are not cast, and kept the castle in the air.

entities.name: William Blackwage, Ralph Raye, Richard Hoope
entities.context: Repeated the two sums and refused to price a barrel.

entities.name: James Burbage
entities.context: Named five pound and a lease, and left both as a sentence.

entities.name: Richard Burbage

entities.name: Thomas Pope
entities.context: Proposed they lower Kemp, and conceded the sentence.

entities.name: Will Kemp
